title: vertiginous golf
text: Hey everyone, just wanted to share my own opinion on this mixed review game. I got this game for free somehow (can't remember how) and i haven't played it a whole lot. but the time that i've spent in it has been enjoyable. I skipped the story, and had no idea there was one until i read other reviews. The game itself is pretty awesome. i like it a lot. Setting: Steampunk minigolf. The controls: Not bad. many people are complaining but it's very simple. left click and move to rotate/move camera, scroll to zoom in/out. hold right click and move back to adjust power and then let go to swing and hit the ball. I have had no problems with the controls, they all seem pretty natural to me. Plus, you get to scout ahead with a steam machine bird so you can plan your shots better. The railings: yeah.. that's one where i have a slight problem with. There are a lack of railings in the game, so many times my ball will fly off of the map. the levels themselves are pretty awesome though. always challenging in one way or another. The Ball: kind of bouncy. it's like a ping pong ball. The Golf Clubs: "you only get to choose from two" - it's minigolf man. you only need one. overall: 7.5/10 - I'd recommend the game for anyone who enjoys minigolf games.

text: A precursor to something like Shadows of Mordor (and a contemporary of the original Assassin's Creed), but at this point dated and not really worth a look unless you're desperate for a (modest) open-world action game. The combat is simple and more limited than newer games of this bent, but fast and fun (without much challenge). Visuals and camera haven't aged too admirably and the loose viking theme lacks imagination and any sort of depth. At best, it's co-opted to provide a structure for bloodshed. Not unenjoyable for a few hours, but once I reached the latter part of the first island I couldn't justify spending more time with it.

title: viking: battle for asgard
text: I can see a little bit of potential in Viking: Battle for Asgard. Although I felt there are a number of things wrong with this game that brought it down into the “not recommended” category. The story, from what I can gather, is that you’re a Viking brought back to fight a Legion army and eventually destroy a woman named Hel. You battle across 4 islands (You re-visit one of them so it’s really only 3 distinct locations) On each island you must raise an army large enough to take over the stronghold, find a rune to summon a dragon and upgrade your weapon. Every island has the same basic objectives and it’s very repetitive. With such vast open areas you think there would be more scenarios, but it’s the same formula 4 times in a row. The gameplay itself is average to below average. The fighting system is clunky which becomes very apparent when you are fighting multiple enemies at once. You end up having to push everyone away from you to separate them out in order to hit them. Otherwise, the surrounding enemies will hit you during your attacks, causing you to be stunned. You are forced to take on a defensive strategy. The extremely narrow FOV also handicaps you as attacks will come blindly. There is a very basic upgrade system of buying new moves and power-ups. There are not any character stats, just collecting gold to buy these things. The extra moves and combos were useful, but I found myself only using the lighting, fire and ice special attacks barely a handful of times during the game. The levels are large but mostly empty. There are a number of fast travel locations in each map, which helps but you’re still required to run around the map discovering them first. Your characters running speed is far too slow for these big distances. The graphics are acceptable and the environment can look quite good. Maybe it was just my game, but I had no in-game music except for the big battles. So most of the time I was listening to my own footsteps. The large battles seem to be the “best” part of the game, but even this is lacking. The battles are great visually. It was awesome to see my large army charging toward the enemy. Ultimately, you are forced to battle on your own to kill Shamans and giants. Thus making the large scale battle seem unnecessary as you and your enemies respawn continually. +Decent graphics +Large scale battles look cool +Large maps (albeit empty) +Environment +Good set of moves to learn +30fps +Clunky combat system +Repetitive gameplay +QTE (quick time events) used excessively +World map lacks zoom or free movement +Narrow FOV +Character run speed too slow +Stealth sections +Voice acting +Small enemy variety This isn’t a game I’d recommend to friends. However, if you’re really into Vikings and hack and slashes, you may want to give this game a try if there is a good sale. Below average

title: viking: battle for asgard
text: In Viking: Battle for Asgard you fill the boots of Skarin, a young Viking Warrior who takes it upon himself to turn the tide against the evil forces of the Underworld and stop the plans of Hel, Goddess of said forces. With the help and guidance of Freya, Skarin will unite the Viking Clans and wage war. Plot wise, I believe Viking is on the weak side. The story, although it's rather simple, it's executed in a weird way and how it progresses further, just leave you either wanting for more or just trying to figure out what the hell happened. The combat however is quite fun and you can be versatile with the various combos you have and although repetitive after a while, it still is fun! Especially the Skirmish Battles are simply epic: it really feels like a battle between armies. Although it's quite old now as a game, it has aged well. However, there are some things that are just terrible, such as the camera is quite unsupportive of your cause and the map is rather hard to use. While there is Fast Travel available, if you miss your queue of spamming the button to enable it, you have to redo it and that is simply annoying. The kill, sneak attack and dodge animations are suburb, but some things, like the blood on Skarin's sword all the time feel a bit unnatural. All in all, Viking is a game that it delivers to do what it set out to do as a game: able to entertain you long enough until you finish that campaign, but I am afraid it leaves no room for replaybility, unless you are hunting down the achievements, although it is possible to do them in one run and be done with it! I would give it a 6/10 rating (Better Than Average Game) ---------------- PROS - Fun combat mechanics with various combos - Battle Arena, where you learn skills and how to utilize them - Skirmish Battles! You need that army, you can't solo it! - Soundtrack, especially the Skirmish Battle Soundtrack! - Challenging combat when it needs to be - Rune Magic is quite fun and powerful - Good graphics - A few details such as the changing terrain when you free an area or uphill and downhill running! CONS - Story is kinda weak - Skarin never talks and doesn't really leave an impression to you - Repetitive combat - Generic quests and no sidequests (unless you count the Beer Delivery Service!) - Map is hard to use - Slow switching from attack to defence - Camera screws up more often than not - Bloody mashing button If you are more of a visual type, I made a video about this one: Thanks for reading folks! Have fun!

title: viking: battle for asgard
text: In this freeroam Action Game with light Stealth Elements you are Skarin, a Viking resurrected by Freya to battle the undead legions of Hel on 3 Islands. You have to rescue your breathren in arms to build an army to reconquer the fallen cities of men. Pros: -Big and epic Battles -Big Maps which will take 4 to 5 hours to complete each -Vikings and Dragons against the undead (which is pretty metal) -Great Soundtrack -Varied Gameplay with Stealth, Platforming, Skirmishes and Battles Cons: -clunky fighting system -unprecise Map without zoom or free movement -stupid story with a horribly bad ending -barebone upgrade system -bad sound design (Players steps sound like hoofs for example, and awful sound mixing) -too much reliance on Quick Time Events (I hate tapping buttons just to open chests or use quicktravel) -battles aren't any form of challenge -awful boss battles -only 3 maps The problem with the showcase of the game, the big battles, is that you don't need any form of strategy or thinking for them. You just need to kill the enemy shamans who pull the undead constantly out of the underworld. If the shamans are killed, the next step in the battle starts. Your own soldiers also get resurrected by your shamans all the time. The soldiers are just there to clatter the battles so you can not advance easily. But you don't need to fight enemy soldiers at all, just the shamans. The whole thing is kinda pointless, and while the first two maps are at least a bit of fun the final one just sucks. I know this is an older game, but I was so disappointed when I finished it, I just had to write this review. Odin's Will this is not.

text: This game is not an open world mmorpg. This isa Dungeon Crawler without the loot. I have been on the game just over 7 hours. I must admit that the game seemed great at first, it is quite fun but soon after you realise the grind. Between level 1 and 20 I just kept doing dungeons, pretty much the same stuff over and over. If this game is supposed to be a Dungeon Crawler game it does fail as I received no loot whatsoever from any of the dungeons I did. All my gear is from the quest reward for doing the dungeon. I would say that the game has the same look feel and combat style as Dynasty Warriors. In short, the game is a hack and slash, it may be great if you have a bunch of friends but doing the same stuff over and over again cannot be that much fun, especially since you get no loot from it. It would have been fun if it had a similar loot system to Diablo or Exile. For a game that advertises itself as "This is unlike any MMORPG you've experienced before." after 6 hours of playing, I will have to pass, I just didn't feel any attraction. Brutal Combat? I am not sure about that. Visual Assault? Sure the main login screen and character creation look amazing but once you are in the game it looks just like every other Korean MMORPG, also the game is locked at 30 FPS Maximum. In Tera after 6 hours I was still playing on (you have plenty of nice fashion in there), so did other games. Even in WoW at level 20 you start seeing some Greens and Blues dropping:)) not to mention the Blues from doing dungeons or quests. If you have nothing else and you want a hack and slash to play with friends go for it, the experience could be rewarding, unfortunately for me I no longer have the same on-line social status that I used to have. I had to play it solo and it was fun only that long before it got boring. Things I did not like: 100000000 of text lines, every single NPC conversation is 100's of lines of 2D text, there are no NPCs to see or talk to. As soon as you get to the location you just get the 2D screen similar to old RPG games. I just kept holding CTRL to skip through and get to the reward part or next mission. Game locked at 30 FPS. Extremely hard to get materials to make anything. Crafting seems confusing and costs too much. Limited character customisation, anything better than the basics will cost you money. This means every character/class you make will look the same considering 5 options for hair styles. No variance in style or armour. A decent outfit would set you back $20. All Premium outfits look the same on all characters/classes, you don't have different looks generic armour either. Empty gameworld, I tried to team up, couldn't do that. You are constrained to cities, I did not see any combat areas outside the cities except for the dungeons. The area outside the cities is just an empty area for you to walk in from A to B. Considering the lack of any NPCs they should have just made you go from city to city by clicking the map or something. You cannot use shared storage until you are level 60 with level 60 characters, so much for twinks. You cannot enchant anything until level 59. The game might get better towards the End Game part (based on what Vishespuppy said in comments) but there is nothing at lower levels to drive any new player to get to the End Game stuff. Better games out there worth your precious time.

text: I'm bad at gardening so I play farm games. I also tend to kill house plants and Viridi is an okay substitute. There's no visual cue as to whether a plant needs water but it'll say "thirsty" when you click it, so you just have to click through them all about once a day. You get a few plants to start and a random plant each week. If you want any more/faster than that, there are microtransactions. From 9-39 cents per seedling. There's also a "cat house" and "nursery" that cost $2.99 and 4.99 respectively. Those let you have extra planters with different settings (I refuse to spend that kind of money on a houseplant simulator so I only know what the ingame descriptions say.) The music is nice but you can also mute it. Won't attract bugs or get your hands dirty.

title: viridi
text: Viridi Is a very simplistic game, a relaxing game that keeps you occupied without giving you a rushed feel. Although there will be in-game purchases you do get a lot out of the free experience. You create a plant pot, each one has its own design and the ability to name it. Every pot comes with its own snail which you can sing to and water just like the plants (I don't really know why you'd water a snail unless snails can get dried up, which I guess they could? You wouldn't want a crusty snail.) Once a week you get one free seedling. These free seedlings are 100% random and give that little feeling of excitement every time you open one. Like most free games, In-Game purchases are a large part in the overall game. Besides the once weekly seedling the only way to get new plants would be to purchase them with (I assume this goes this goes w/o saying) real money. This has not bothered me too much as you can still get the relaxing part of the game down, although it can get rather bothersome to know every individual plant would come out of your paycheck. If you reall get into the game, I'm sure you wouldn't regret purchasing some plants or new areas. One thing that really keeps you on your toes is the wait for your seedlings to up and have ther little spurts of growth. The growth of your succulent brings out the ultimate reward in Viridi. Although patience is key, it does not come w/o its hardships and rewards, which I think Viridi expresses perfectly. I'm personally very attached to succulents and have friends who do enjoy plants just as much as I, and because of that I would recommend this game. Viridi is a good game, one that I'd love to see others enjoy and although this game is not without its flaws I liked Viridi and I'm sure many others do aswell.
